card.name: Linking words before a named co-drug
card.fires_on: Small linking words (of, when, either, a comma) right before a second drug is named in drug-interaction statements, e.g. 'pharmacokinetics of warfarin'. A few hits are the same kind of word in general prose, e.g. 'is not English'.

modes.label: Interaction sentences
modes.description: A linking word just before the affected drug's name in text about effects on another drug's levels or clearance.
modes.example: Mirtazapine did not significantly affect the pharmacokinetics<< of>> phenytoin.

modes.label: Co-administration lists
modes.description: A comma or 'when' just before a further drug in a list of co-administered drugs.
modes.example: studies have been carried out with treprostinil (oral or subcutaneous) co-administered with acetaminophen (4 g/day<<),>> warfarin (25 mg/day

modes.label: Non-drug prose
modes.description: Linking words in general text where a noun is expected next.
modes.example: This act also required proficiency<< of>> the English language.

card.writes: It seems to push the model toward naming a specific substance next (e.g. lithium, caffeine, mercury) and away from other word types.
card.plain: It fires on the small word that comes just before a second drug is named in interaction text.
